To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the seeds of Canavalia cathartaica and Canavilia maritima are spherical in shape, have higher sphericity than corresponding kernels, have lower porosity than kernels and have higher rupture force and energy for kernels than seeds.
the seeds of Canavalia catharctica and C. maritina are of similar size, shape and mechanical strength.
the physical and mechanical characteristics of seeds and kernels are important to understand the behaviour of Canavalia grains during harvesting, handling, storage, processing and utilization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical and mechanical characterization of the seeds and kernels of the wild Canavalia species of coastal sand dune of Southwest India.
the basic and complex geometrical properties of Canavalia seed and kernel.
the design, development and evaluation of the physical and mechanical characteristics of Canavalia species of coastal sand dune of Southwest India.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
seeds of Canavalia possess higher values of geometric and mechanical properties than kernels and seeds of C. Cathartica possess higher values than C. maratima.

seeds of Canavalia catharitca and Canavalia martiima are of medium size, low bulk density, high porosity, high sphericity, low angle of repose, low static coefficient of friction, high rupture force and rupture energy, low moisture content and high oil content and hence can be processed using the equipments and methods used for processing similar sized legume seeds.
seeds of Canavalia are more suitable for harvesting, sorting, processing and handling than kernels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Canavalia seeds can be handled and processed in the conventional equipments designed for legume seeds.
the seeds of Canavalia are suitable for mechanical processing.
the Canavalia seeds are hard and strong, while the kernels are soft and weak.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the seeds and kernels of both Canavalia species can be handled and processed using conventional equipment.
the seeds of C. Cathartica and C. maritma can be handled, sorted and processed in similar
Canavalia seeds can be processed in existing food industries and can be used in the development of new products.
